Help

Frequently asked questions

Last updated 30 October 2026 · The same answers you'll find in the app, under Help › FAQs

Do I need to connect my bank account?

No. Duolign works entirely from figures you type in or bank statements you upload. You never give Duolign access to your bank, and it can never move money.

How does the payday split work?

Each payday, Duolign works out what each of you puts towards your bills, budgets and debts, using the split your household chose: half each, by income, or a custom split. It then shows exactly what to transfer and where.

You make the transfers yourselves and mark them done. Duolign never moves money.

What if we don't split everything 50/50?

You choose how shared costs are split: half each, in proportion to your incomes, or a custom split such as 60/40. Either of you can propose a change from Household, and it takes effect once the other agrees.

Each of you also has a personal allowance: money that's yours to spend, with no need to account for it.

What if one of our incomes doesn't stretch to its share, or we're over our combined income?

Nobody is ever asked to transfer more than they earn, and each of your payday lists adds up to your own income exactly.

If one income doesn't stretch to its share in a month, the split rebalances: first the shares of your budgets, then the shares of the shared bills, and only then does money go straight into the other account. Allowances stay equal and whole whenever there's a surplus. Each step is explained in one line about that month, never as one of you covering the other.

If your combined income doesn't cover the month, Duolign says so plainly, with the amount, and takes it from your budgets so every bill is still paid. You can choose together which budgets it comes from.

What's the difference between a bill and a budget?

A bill is a fixed payment that leaves on a schedule, like rent, energy, council tax or a phone contract. Each account you pay bills from has its own Bills, named after it, such as Joint current - Bills.

A budget is money set aside for spending that changes month to month, like groceries, petrol or eating out. You choose which budgets you have, and you can add your own. Until you set an amount, a budget uses what you spent in it last month.

When you bring in a statement, Duolign spots your bills for you and remembers where each shop's spending goes, so most of each month sorts itself.

What if one of us is paid weekly, or our pay changes month to month?

Each of you sets your own payday: monthly (on a set date, or a day like the last Friday of the month), weekly or fortnightly. It works when you're paid on different schedules.

If your pay varies too much to predict, choose irregular, and you set each month's amounts yourselves.

Can I use Duolign on my own, without a partner?

Duolign is built for two people sharing household costs, so a household always has two of you.

If only one of you wants to do the day-to-day, choose "Just me" under Household › Who runs payday. You confirm both incomes and mark both sets of transfers yourself, and your partner keeps a login to see everything. That also works if you've invited your partner and they haven't joined yet.

Can my partner see everything I enter?

Mostly, yes: your bills, budgets, debts, savings and joint accounts are shared between you; that's the point of a shared household.

You can keep one of your own accounts private from your partner (tap it on Accounts). Its transactions and balance stay yours, and any shared costs paid from it are still split fairly.

Privacy mode (Settings › Privacy & Security) also hides figures on screen, for example in public, without changing what's shared.

Which banks work with statement upload?

Any UK bank. Upload the PDF statement or CSV export your bank gives you, or type the figures in by hand instead.

How accurate is statement reading?

Duolign reads each transaction off your statement, then checks what it found against the statement's own printed totals before anything is saved. A statement that doesn't add up is rejected rather than imported wrong.

Either way, check what's been imported before relying on it.

One of my bank's pots has its own card. How do I include what I spend from it?

Some banks let a pot have its own card, such as a Monzo regular pot with a virtual card. What you spend with that card appears only on the pot's own statement. Your account's statement just shows money moving to and from the pot.

Upload the pot's statement under its account, choose One of its pots, then pick the pot. Its card spending then counts, and the money moved between the pot and the account is left out, so nothing is counted twice. Pots without their own statement work as before.

On Monzo: from Home, open the pot linked to the card. Tap the settings icon or the three dots at the top right of the pot, choose Pot documents (or Statements and documents), then Pot statement. Pick the dates and download it.

What happens if I delete a statement?

Its transactions go with it, along with everything recorded about them: where they were sorted, income confirmed from them, loan payments linked to them and bills matched to them. Your figures go back to how they would be if you had never uploaded it.

So you can upload it again, to the same account or a different one, without anything being counted twice. Anything you taught Duolign about a shop stays, so its transactions are recognised again.

Is Duolign free? What does Premium add?

The free plan includes the payday split, bills, budgets, savings, investments, debts, statement upload and three months of trends.

Premium adds your full payday history, longer trends and forecasts, the What-If Simulator and debt strategy comparison. It's £5.99 a month or £49.99 a year, and one subscription covers both of you.

Is my data safe, and where is it stored?

Your data is encrypted in transit and at rest, stored in the EU, and never sold or used for advertising.

You can protect your sign-in with two-factor authentication and lock the app with Face ID, your fingerprint or a PIN. Every company that helps run Duolign is listed on the Security & Encryption page at duolign.co.uk.

Will I get notifications?

Only if you allow them. Duolign lets you know when your partner asks for your OK on a change, when your pay has been confirmed, when a statement is due to upload, and when something needs filling in, such as a debt's details or your typical monthly spend.

Turn them off any time in Settings › Notifications & Activity.

What happens if we split up, or one of us leaves?

Either of you can delete just your own account. Your login and private data are erased, and the household stays for the other person.

Or you can delete the whole household, for both of you. Either way it happens 30 days later, and you can cancel until then.

How do I request the removal of my data?

If you still have the app, the fastest way is in-app: Settings › Privacy & Security › Delete this household or Delete my account. Both permanently erase your data 30 days later (cancellable from the same screen until then), and either way you can export your data first. See our Privacy Policy for exactly what each one erases.

Don't have the app installed, or would rather not? Use the Delete My Data form instead. This isn't instant: we verify it's really you before erasing anything, same as any other request to delete a real household's financial data, but we'll follow up at the email you give us.

Open the Delete My Data form

Can I get a copy of my data?

Yes. Go to Settings › Data & Storage and tap Download my data. You get a zip file of your household's data and your own private data; your partner's private data isn't included.
